title: indigo_prop_tool: add -f/--full-text to print long and multiline text values in whole
description:
Owner request (2026-11-28). indigo_prop_tool prints only the first TEXT_LEN_TO_PRINT (80) characters of a text item followed by '+ N characters' (indigo_tools/indigo_prop_tool.c, around line 403), in both list and get output, so long or multiline values such as the scheduler's AGENT_SCHEDULER_HISTORY.ENTRIES (text, one line per run, ticket b4808d4d) or the task bodies AGENT_SCHEDULER_TASK_n.TASK cannot be read from the command line.

Expected: a new option -f / --full-text (check it does not collide with existing options -e -b -l -r -p -T -t -w -s -h) prints text values in whole, including embedded newlines, for list, get and the wait/track modes wherever text values are printed. Without the option the output stays exactly as now (80-character cut), so existing scripts are unaffected. Choose a readable format for multiline values (e.g. print the value verbatim inside the quotes, newlines kept) and document it in --help and in indigo_docs/PROPERTY_MANIPULATION.md (and update the scheduler docs that now say the full history must be read in a client, if ticket b4808d4d has landed). Add tests in the existing prop_tool test suite (indigo_test/unit/test_prop_tool_parser.c or similar) for a long single-line value, a multiline value, and the default cut unchanged. Keep the code portable (Linux, macOS, Windows).

outcome.summary:
Product code and docs are correct. One test-coverage defect needs fixing.

Verified: indigo_tools/indigo_prop_tool.c:1019 parses -f/--full-text without clashing with -e -b -l -r -p -T -t -w -s -h (and -r/-p/-T/-t/-w still consume their argument first). Every text value goes through print_property_list (:404, also used for set output and -w at :851/:861, -e labels and the -s prefix) or print_property_get_filtered (:502), and both honour print_full_text. Without -f both branches are unchanged byte for byte. indigo_get_text_item_value() returns long_value when set, so values over INDIGO_VALUE_SIZE print in whole. text_value[] (:485) points into the callback's property, which stays valid until the printf loop at :560 in the same synchronous call; nothing in between frees it, so the lifetime is safe. Removing static from print_property_get_filtered (:481) matches print_property_list and print_property_list_state, which are already exported. No other definition exists in indigo_libs, and it builds into the executable only. The multiline format (verbatim, quotes not escaped, closing quote and '  # label' after the last line, -s prefix once per item) follows from the code. PROPERTY_MANIPULATION.md documents it, and its default-cut example is arithmetically right (68+12=80, 143-80=63, blank line from the existing extra newline). --help, PROPERTY_MANIPULATION.md, INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md:120,1358 and SCHEDULER.md:431 agree. Portable: plain printf, nothing platform-specific. I rebuilt test_prop_tool_parser.c myself with -Wall -Wextra (no new warnings in indigo_prop_tool.c) and with ASan/UBSan: 8/8 pass.

Defect (test coverage regression): indigo_test/unit/test_prop_tool_parser.c:321. full_text_output now runs before list_output and leaves print_full_text=true; the runner has no way to reset it. So list_output's existing plain and extended TEXT assertions ('Dev.TEXT.ITEM = "value"') now go through the new -f branch (indigo_prop_tool.c:404) and no longer reach the default short

Round 2 (6736b923e, tree 741e4fee4): the round-1 coverage defect is fixed. Nothing blocks.

Coverage restored: test_prop_tool_parser.c:287-291. full_text_output first checks a short value in default mode (list 'Dev.TEXT.ITEM = "value"\n', get 'value\n'), so the default short-text branch indigo_prop_tool.c:409-410 and the default get branch are exercised again. :319 resets print_full_text at the end of the case. :216 resets it again at the start of list_output, so list_output's plain and extended text checks go through the default path even if full_text_output stops early on a failed assert. The default checks run before enable_full_text(), so they can only pass through the default branches.

Exporting print_full_text (indigo_prop_tool.c:54) is acceptable. The file already exports test hooks and globals with external linkage: is_connected (:966), the parse_* functions, read_file, process_quotes, print_property_list, print_property_list_state and print_property_get_filtered. nm on build/lib/libindigo_client.a finds no print_full_text, and grep finds no other definition in the tree, so neither the prop_tool binary nor the unit-test link can clash. The tool sets the flag only in option parsing (:1020), so its behaviour does not change.

Doc: PROPERTY_MANIPULATION.md:207-208 now says that with -s the [STATE] prefix appears only on the first line. That matches the code: the prefix is printed once per item at :399, and only without -e, where it appears at all.

Verified myself: I rebuilt test_prop_tool_parser.c with -Wall (no warnings in indigo_prop_tool.c) and with ASan/UBSan. Both gave 8/8 PASS, and full_text_output also passes when run alone (INDIGO_TEST_CASE_FILTER). Recorded checks whitespace and unit pass on the current tree. The ad-hoc command-1 check (make -C indigo_test test-tool-input-safety) is recorded as failing on this tree. Its 3 failures are the baseline Python cases tracked in ticket 2b46dfdb, not this change. flow status therefore still lists 'A check fai
